Recorded from atlc 27b912a against algotradelib a08fb97, in a copy of this directory holding the store `make-store store` writes (tests/make-store.cpp), with CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH naming the library.
NAME.json is the stdout of `atlc run NAME.toml` for wide, limit and store; limit.fills.csv is the file `atlc run limit.toml --fills limit.fills.csv` wrote.
NAME.args is the args of `atlc spec NAME.toml --json`, one per line.
errors.txt holds, for bad-date, wide-order, bound and missing, the spec's name, a tab, and the `error:` line `atlc run NAME.toml` printed on stderr.
store.toml and missing.toml were run with `duckdb = '<DuckDB's directory>'` under `[build]` added.
Every path of the copy is written @DIR@.
wide-close.csv and kr-daily.csv are synthetic; kr-daily.csv gaps up every ninth day, so some limits expire.
Only an atlc that still has `atlc run` and `atlc spec` (27b912a) can record them again.
wide.toml read `fill = "open-prev-close"` when recorded; that fill is gone, and it now names `decision-close.hpp` as its market-price rule, which fills at the same prices.
wide.json is the recording with the two caveats the rule adds (`market_price_rule`, `market_fills_by_rule`), and wide.args without `replay.fill`.
On 2026-11-06 wide.toml gave the header for `fill = "decision-close"`, the library's rule with the same body: by hand, wide.json's `market_price_rule` became `decision-close` (the header named its function, `decision_close`) and wide.args gained `replay.fill=decision-close`; decision-close.hpp stays for the acceptance case of a header rule.
On 2026-11-05 every `data.*` argument in the `.args` files and every `[data]` table in the `.toml` files was renamed `bars.*` and `[bars]` by hand, when the run spec's `[data]` table became `[bars]`; no report or error changed.
